project: Automatos AI — PRD-251 Socials, Wave 0 (the gate, the tables, the API, the prerequisite fixes, and the bare Socials tab)
description: Wave 0 of PRD-251 (docs/PRDS/PRD-251-SOCIALS.md, decisions D1-D15 binding; owner answers of 2026-09-23 recorded in its status block). Branch feat/prd-251-socials <- main af214bc7b in its own worktree (<workspace>/.worktrees/automatos-ai/feat+prd-251-socials). Nine stories: S0.1 config and switches, S0.2 tables and migration, S0.3 service and API, S0.4 three prerequisite fixes (LinkedIn cross-tenant, video in Deliverables, image-store lookup), S0.5 the bare Socials tab, and S0.6 the platform-wide Composio deny list (PRD-251 is Composio-first since 2026-09-23: customers connect media tools in Composio and agents use them). Every plan gets Socials (no plan key). Nothing here renders media, schedules jobs or publishes to a channel — those are Waves 1-3 and start only after the owner has tested this wave on the socials stack.

userStories.title: S0.1 — Config, the two Socials switches and the approve permission
userStories.description: Gate everything Socials behind two switches (D1, owner 2026-09-23: every plan gets Socials, so there is NO plan exposure key). (a) orchestrator/config.py gains, in one commented 'PRD-251 Socials' group: SOCIALS_ENABLED_DEFAULT (bool, env, default False), SOCIALS_MEDIA_URL_TTL_SECONDS=86400, SOCIALS_MISFIRE_GRACE_SECONDS=1800, SOCIALS_MAX_TARGET_ATTEMPTS=3, SOCIALS_RENDER_URL='', SOCIALS_PUBLIC_MEDIA_BUCKET=''. Env reads happen only in config.py. (b) New package modules/socials/ with settings.py mirroring modules/voice/live_settings.py: socials_master_enabled() reads the 'socials'/'enabled' system setting through core.llm.manager.get_system_setting with the default taken from config.SOCIALS_ENABLED_DEFAULT; parse_workspace_socials(settings) -> WorkspaceSocials(enabled: bool); validate_socials_update(value) fail-closed (only the key 'enabled', a bool); and a FastAPI dependency require_socials_enabled that raises 404 unless BOTH the master switch and the caller's workspace switch are on. userStories.title: S0.3a — The socials service: status machine, content hash, approval and the publish guard
userStories.description: modules/socials/service.py owns the post lifecycle as pure, tested logic. (a) The status machine: an explicit allowed-transitions table over the D2 statuses; an illegal transition raises IllegalTransition. Wave 0 transitions: draft -> needs_approval (submit); changes_requested -> needs_approval (submit); needs_approval -> approved | changes_requested | archived (reject); approved -> scheduled (schedule) -> approved (unschedule); approved|scheduled -> needs_approval (any content edit). Rendering, publishing, missed and failed transitions arrive with their waves. (b) compute_content_hash(post): sha256 over canonical JSON (sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) of copy, variables, sources, format, template_id and media. Docstring: Wave 1 extends 'media' with the rendered files' digests. (c) create_draft, update_post (recomputes the hash; if an approved or scheduled post's hash changes, status -> needs_approval and the approval is void because approved_hash != content_hash), submit, approve(user, override_unsourced=False), request_changes(user, comment), reject(user, reason), schedule(scheduled_for, timezone), unschedule. Every review action appends to review_log. (d) D7: unsourced_claims(post) returns the names of variables with claim=true that have no entry in sources. approve raises UnsourcedClaims(names) unless override_unsourced=True, in which case override_unsourced is stored and the review_log entry names the claims. (e) assert_publishable(post) raises NotPublishable unless status is approved or scheduled AND approved_hash == content_hash. (f) modules/socials/publisher.py: publish_post(db, post) calls assert_publishable FIRST, then — Wave 0 has no channel publishers — raises PublishingUnavailable. This is the seam S3.3 fills; nothing in it calls Composio yet.

userStories.title: S0.3b — The /api/socials routes behind the gate
userStories.description: api/socials.py: GET /api/socials/posts?status=&from=&to=; POST /api/socials/posts; GET and PATCH /api/socials/posts/{id}; POST /api/socials/posts/{id}/submit|approve|request-changes|reject|schedule|unschedule|publish-now. Mount it the way other routers are mounted (grep main.py's include_router list). Every route depends on require_socials_enabled (US-001) and on the caller's workspace; every query filters by that workspace_id, so another workspace's post is a 404. approve additionally requires 'socials:approve' (403 otherwise). Write permissions otherwise mirror api/blog.py. Exceptions map: IllegalTransition -> 409, UnsourcedClaims -> 422 (body names the claims), NotPublishable -> 409, PublishingUnavailable -> 501 with 'Channel publishing arrives in Wave 3'. Add a guard test that walks the app's routes under /api/socials and asserts each carries require_socials_enabled, so a later route cannot skip the gate. Update orchestrator/reports/route-manifest.json for every new route, plus PUT /api/workspaces/current/socials (CI's frontend route-contract reads the COMMITTED manifest): regenerate with `cd orchestrator && python3 -m scripts.dump_routes`, or hand-edit sorted by (path, method) and bump route_count.

userStories.title: S0.4c — The image-store public lookup and Range streaming
userStories.description: GET /api/generated-images/{id} (api/generated_images.py:23-28) calls image_store.get_image(image_id, workspace_id=None), which lists the prefix and falls back to one list_objects_v2 call with MaxKeys=1000 (core/services/image_store.py:69-94) — past 1000 objects lookups start returning 404 — and then reads the whole object into memory (:100). Fix both: (a) on save, also write a small pointer object (or a lookup row — pick the smaller change and say why) mapping image_id -> key, and resolve by that pointer with one GET; legacy ids without a pointer fall back to a PAGINATED listing (ContinuationToken or a paginator), never a single 1000-key page; (b) the route streams the body and honours Range: bytes=a-b with 206, Content-Range, Accept-Ranges and Content-Length, using S3 get_object(Range=...). Socials media never uses this route (D9); this fixes the platform defect the PRD found.

userStories.title: S0.6 — The Composio deny list, platform-wide
userStories.description: PRD-251 is Composio-first (D12/D15/D16): customers connect paid media tools in Composio and agents use them. Composio's Higgsfield toolkit (higgsfield_mcp) carries HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CONFIRM_BILLING_PURCHASE, which Composio documents as 'charges real money', and Automatos has no guard: no per-action allow/deny list, no billing keyword in modules/tools/capabilities/classifier.py, and the policy plane that enforces REQUIRES_CONFIRMATION ships 'off' (config.py:898). Add a deny list of Composio action slugs stored as a system setting ('composio' / 'denied_actions', a JSON list), made settable in Settings -> System Settings the same way US-001 made socials.enabled settable, and seeded with the eight D16 slugs: HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CONFIRM_BILLING_PURCHASE, HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CANCEL_TRIAL_AUTO_RENEWAL, HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CONFIRM_TRIAL_CANCEL, HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CREATE_WEBSITE, HIGGSFIELD_MCP_DEPLOY_WEBSITE, HIGGSFIELD_MCP_PUBLISH_WEBSITE, HIGGSFIELD_MCP_PARTICIPATE_IN_CONTEST, HIGGSFIELD_MCP_APPS_INVOKE. EVERY path that executes a Composio action consults it before any network call — ComposioToolExecutor.execute (core/composio/tool_executor.py:344), api/recipe_executor.py and api/composio.py are known; grep for the rest (execute_action, tools.execute, client execute calls) — and refuses with 'This action is blocked in Automatos: <reason>'. It never depends on the policy plane mode or on the capability classifier. Slug matching is case-insensitive. Put the check in ONE helper that every entry point calls; do not copy it.
acceptanceCriteria: With AUTOMATOS_POLICY_PLANE=off, executing HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CONFIRM_BILLING_PURCHASE through each entry point returns the blocked error and the Composio client (mocked) is never called — tests/test_prd251_composio_deny.py.
Removing the slug from the system setting unblocks it with no restart or deploy (test).
A test lists every Composio execution entry point found by grep and proves each one calls the single deny-list helper.
The seeded setting holds the eight D16 slugs and is visible to the super-admin in Settings -> System Settings.
CI green on the story's commit for the five PRD-251 jobs; record the run id.

Composio docs verified 2026-09-23: docs.composio.dev/toolkits/higgsfield_mcp. The list is DATA (system setting), never a code constant.
